conventions: English phrasal particles in this psalm — eat up (27.2), lift up (27.5, 27.6), take up (27.10), put away and cast off (27.9), deliver over and risen up (27.12) — are kept inside the verb's unit under rule 44, discontinuous around the object where the ASV interposes it, on the reading that the bare English verb does not write the source verb's whole lexeme (אכל as consuming, אסף as gathering in, נטה hiphil as removing, רום polel/qal as exalting, נתן as delivering over). The one close call is 27.2's 'eat up', where marking 'up' added under rule 44's surplus-particle sentence was the competing reading and is named in the unit note; the chapter treats the whole family one way.

The two 'Even's are deliberately different: 27.2 'Even mine adversaries' stands before an asyndetic appositive with no waw and no marker on the phrase and is added (rules 14, 16), while 27.3 'Even then' is the ASV's one adverbial rendering of the written בְּזֹאת and is aligned to those two morphemes under rules 30/40, headed on זֹאת, with the alternative ('then' on זֹאת, 'Even' added, בְּ unrepresented) named in the note. A later reader should not read 27.3 as folding an unlicensed 'Even' to avoid an added unit.
report: Read all 14 verses end to end against the candidate table. Every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one morpheme differently in different clauses (suffix my/me/mine/I by case; בְּ in/upon/unto/against/when by context; לְ of/unto/to; יהוה with or without vocative O or rectum of; וְ and/also/yea/then/And-now), and each difference is licensed by the printed English. No construction was analysed two ways.

Checked the hidden split the table cannot see: the five added units (A Psalm 27.1, Even 27.2, when 27.7, When thou saidst 27.8, I had fainted 27.13) against English folded into a morpheme elsewhere. 27.2's appositional Even (no waw, no marker on the phrase) is added under rules 14/16 while 27.3's 'Even then' rests on the written בְּזֹאת under rule 30/40 with the alternative named in the note; 27.7's when subordinates an asyndetic finite clause (rule 55) while 27.4's That is the finite recasting of a bare infinitive construct with its own subject suffix (rule 52's bare-infinitive reasoning), the note naming the alternative. These are different constructions, not a split.

Phrasal particles are handled uniformly across the chapter: eat up (27.2), lift up (27.5, 27.6), take up (27.10), put away and cast off (27.9), deliver over and risen up (27.12) all stay with the verb under rule 44, with the surplus-particle alternative noted where it was close (27.2). Recorded as a convention rather than changed.

BSB disagreements: the four R tokens (מִ 27.1 'Whom', לִי 27.2, בְּ after חֲזוֹת 27.4 and רְאוֹת 27.13) and the 27.2 suffix are all rule 40 recastings the ASV writes bare; BSB attaches the preposition to its phrase by its own convention. None is an error. Nothing changed for the aggregate.

Rule 29's attributive-rectum determiner is applied the same way in 27.11 (a plain path: 'a' on the construct) and 27.12 (false witnesses: no determiner), and the supplied 'the' on construct nouns (27.1, 27.4, 27.5, 27.12, 27.13) is consistent. No promotions or amendments: the chapter taught nothing the contract does not already say.
